title: A Hess intermediate used twice
statement:
Given $\ce{A -> B}$ with $\Delta H=-35$ kJ and $\ce{2B -> C}$ with $\Delta H=+84$ kJ, find the heat for $\ce{2A -> C}$.

[_]{a}

explanations: Two copies of the first step cancel two B.
The first step was included only once.
This is the reverse net reaction.
The first step was given the wrong sign.

hints: Match the amount of B formed and consumed.
solution: Double the first step to create two B and $-70$ kJ. Add the unmodified second step: $-70+84=14$ kJ.
